characters.description: One of seven former Tower climbers establishing a new world together. Max shares leadership of the human capital with his wife, Tanila, while the founders connect their peoples to a common divine system.
characters.name: Max Hoste

characters.description: An elven world champion, one of the seven founders, and Max's wife. She shares the human capital with him as the group begins creating and guiding its peoples. Their marriage makes the new divine undertaking a family responsibility as well as a joint mission.
characters.name: Tanila

characters.description: A dwarven world champion and one of the seven founders of the new world. She is part of the close group jointly responsible for its peoples and development. Like the other champions, she is linked to a created race whose progress contributes to divine growth.
characters.name: Batrire

characters.description: A dwarven world champion and one of the seven allies founding the new world. He begins this divine undertaking alongside Batrire and their longtime companions. The group's shared system ties his future advancement to the progress of the people under his care.
characters.name: Fowl Hammerfall

characters.description: An elven world champion and member of the seven-person founding group. She helps establish the shared world and assumes responsibility for one of its created peoples. She enters godhood within a cooperative structure that gives every capital its own herald.
characters.name: Cordelia

characters.description: A dragon world champion and one of the seven founders of the new world. He represents the dragons as the group begins creating and guiding its peoples.
characters.name: Rakonath

characters.description: A demon world champion and one of the seven founders of the new world. He shares responsibility for creating the world and guiding its demon people.
characters.name: Bound demon companion

characters.description: A rabbit-shaped administrative assistant assigned to System 401. The helper guides the seven founders through world design and explains the first rules governing divine points, protection, champions, and arenas.
characters.name: System helper

characters.description: Max's adviser, who warns that Max must advance rapidly before outside threats can reach the new world and endanger his family. Bob urges him to seek a much higher divine tier during the available protection period.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: An enchantress serving as the bound demon companion's herald. She administers his proclamations and carries out his early requests for resources as he begins reorganizing the demon capital.
characters.name: Demon herald

characters.description: The newborn child of Max and Tanila, carried by Tanila during the Tower ascent. Her unusual sensitivity to System magic is apparent immediately, leaving her parents concerned that distant gods may notice her significance or regard her as a threat.
characters.name: Max and Tanila's daughter

characters.description: A long-lived arena challenger who controls many worlds and has extensive experience fighting other gods. He targets Max after Max loses personal protection and relies on accumulated divine points to sustain his strength.
characters.name: Rock-bodied god

characters.description: Max's chosen human bloodline heir and the appointed king of the human capital. His transformation gives him greater physical power, and he pledges to serve both the people and Max.
characters.name: Human king

characters.description: A neighboring water-domain goddess who protects two aquatic peoples sharing an underwater world. She asks Max to help defend them from an approaching tier-seven god.
characters.name: Aquatic goddess

characters.description: A tier-seven god preparing to claim the underwater world shared by the aquatic goddess and the two peoples under her protection.
characters.name: Tier-seven invader

characters.description: A powerful water god preparing to invade the underwater world shared by two aquatic peoples. The aquatic goddess expects him to arrive with forces from his own world and asks Max to help organize the defense.
characters.name: Tier-seven leviathan

characters.description: A huge lava-domain demon reached by Max's summoning spell and connected to the bound demon companion's past. The spell prevents him from attacking Max, and his attempts to violate that protection leave him owing a System-enforced debt.
characters.name: Demon king

characters.description: A flying god whom Max challenges despite reports of an ability that can alter reality. His unknown magic and aerial advantage make the coming arena encounter difficult for Max and his allies to predict.
characters.name: Crow god

characters.description: A disciplined six-armed demon chosen as the bound demon companion's bloodline heir and daughter. She becomes queen of the demon people and is charged with enforcing reforms based on cooperation.
characters.name: Demon queen

characters.description: A dwarf fighter selected by Fowl and Batrire to rule their capital alongside his healer wife. The married pair receive divine bloodlines and sparks and are charged with leading dwarven dungeon and Tower efforts.
characters.name: Dwarven king

characters.description: A dwarf healer selected by Fowl and Batrire to rule their capital alongside her fighter husband. The married pair receive divine bloodlines and sparks and are charged with leading dwarven dungeon and Tower efforts.
characters.name: Dwarven queen

characters.description: A resilient elven fighter appointed by Cordelia as the first queen of Ember Grove. After surviving a mental assault and protecting her dungeon party, she receives Cordelia's bloodline and a divine spark that can extend a protective ward across the capital.
characters.name: Elven queen

characters.description: A juvenile red dragon who brings Rakonath a fish before joining the younger dragons' flight instruction.
characters.name: Red dragon companion

characters.description: An elder blue dragon appointed by Rakonath to lead a new guardian flight. The alpha is responsible for selecting representatives from different age groups to share Rakonath's bloodline spark as the dragons prepare to defend others.
characters.name: Dragon flight alpha

characters.description: An immense demon drawn into Max's summoning domain during his daughter's catastrophic awakening. The entity recognizes Max, claims to have been waiting for him, and appears while an unknown force is threatening the child's life.
characters.name: Immense summoned demon

characters.description: The immense summoned demon is Death, one of the Nine. Bob warns that Max cannot defeat this primordial entity, which threatens Max's daughter and claims sole power to release her from the awakening trap.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: The frontline demon warrior in the five-person cross-kingdom champion party. Linked rings connect the warrior with Max and Tanila's daughter, a red dragon, a dwarf healer, and an elven elemental mage as they prepare for the Tower.
characters.name: Champion party demon warrior

characters.description: The dwarf healer in the five-person cross-kingdom champion party. Linked rings connect the healer with Max and Tanila's daughter, a red dragon, a demon warrior, and an elven elemental mage as they prepare for the Tower.
characters.name: Champion party dwarven healer

characters.description: The elemental mage in the five-person cross-kingdom champion party. Linked rings connect the mage with Max and Tanila's daughter, a red dragon, a demon warrior, and a dwarf healer as they prepare for the Tower.
characters.name: Champion party elven mage

characters.description: The tier-four authority among four avian gods attacking people on a world claimed by Max. The owl-like god detects Max's arrival, stops the massacre when he approaches openly, and takes control of the negotiation.
characters.name: Owl-like avian god

characters.description: An aggressive avian god participating in the assault on people tied to Max's claim. The falcon god confronts Max during the attempted settlement but answers to the stronger owl-like leader, who can halt the attack and control the negotiation.
characters.name: Falcon god

characters.description: The red dragon companion in the five-member champion party led by Max and Tanila's daughter. Shalespark can assume a red-haired humanoid form and joins the group as it prepares for the dangerous dungeons before the Tower.
characters.name: Shalespark

characters.description: Max and Tanila's daughter, who leads a party of five chosen champions. The gods equip the group and permit them to pursue two dangerous dungeon rewards ahead of the Tower.
characters.name: Mirana

characters.description: An immense gold dragon who controls a boon in a dangerous pre-Tower dungeon. He first offers the champion party its reward without battle, then makes the death of its dragon member the condition for receiving it.
characters.name: Gold dragon god

characters.description: A trusted divine ally who summons Max for a confidential meeting after learning of the gold dragon's interest. Restrictions prevent an ordinary explanation, so he seeks a safer way to share what he knows.
characters.name: Human god adviser

characters.description: A longstanding ally of the human god adviser. He joins the restricted meeting when the gold dragon is mentioned and helps devise a written method for communicating information that cannot safely be spoken.
characters.name: Dwarven god adviser

characters.description: The current leader of Max's former Golden Axe faction, having succeeded Everett after his death. Tom recognizes Max beneath his disguise during a secret return and quietly directs him toward his family without exposing the visit.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: Max's sister, reunited with him beside their dying mother during his covert return. Fifteen local years have passed, and Stacy now has children in her household and signs of growing personal power.
characters.name: Stacy

characters.description: Max's mother, whom he finds near death after making a prohibited return to his original world.
characters.name: Max's mother

characters.description: A world-eating god who renews an earlier challenge against Max and threatens another of his worlds. The helper identifies this kind of opponent as a danger that most gods would avoid confronting directly.
characters.name: Void god challenger

characters.description: An elderly gnome who tends a world previously rescued by Max and speaks for its four protectors. He takes Max into a private discussion about the promised reward and Max's request for help against a void god.
characters.name: Elderly gnome caretaker

characters.description: Max's returning contact on a world he previously saved, now serving in a comfortable official position. The dwarf reports turnover among the council and cautions that its new members might ask Max to substantiate his claim.
characters.name: Dwarf liaison

characters.description: An arena official who detects Max's false black-hole-bomb threat after the void god surrenders. The administrator agrees to conceal the bluff if Max accepts the badly damaged world awarded by the match.
characters.name: Arena administrator

recaps.ending: Max defeats the void god without a usable anti-void weapon, sustaining a fake black-hole-bomb threat until the challenger surrenders. The void god admits that its father ordered both attacks but does not identify him. Max accepts a badly damaged world and keeps the bluff secret. The winnings let Max reach tier four and become Godbound, while Tanila, Batrire, Fowl, Cordelia, Rakonath, and the bound demon companion reach tier three. The seven postpone a portal pad until all can defend their world with tier-five domains, and Max continues racing toward tier six before the expected clash among black-skill holders. Max and Tanila's daughter and her red dragon companion have reconciled after losing three teammates on Tower floor 55 and are climbing again with a rebuilt party. Death remains bound by a twenty-five-thousand-year nonaggression oath, but the Nine, the gold dragon god, the demon king's debt, and the identity of the power directing Max's enemies remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Max, Tanila, and their five fellow former climbers become gods and found a shared world, but Max's earlier victories end his protection and force him into arena conflicts. He defeats a rock god and a falcon god, accepts a crow god's surrender, and survives a far stronger leviathan while losing an allied goddess. As the founders build linked societies, Max and Tanila's exceptional daughter survives an awakening trap set by Death, bonds permanently with a young red dragon, and later loses three party members on Tower floor 55 before rebuilding her team. Max also returns secretly to his original world to say goodbye to his dying mother. In the final arena challenge, he bluffs a void god with an imitation black-hole bomb and wins its surrender. Max reaches tier four, the other founders reach tier three, and the group delays cross-realm travel while preparing for tier-five defenses and a coming conflict involving the three black skills and the Nine.

recaps.text: Previously: Max and his companions survived the Tower together and emerged as champions. The group includes Tanila, Batrire, Fowl, Cordelia, Rakonath, a bound demon companion, and Bob, the black skill bonded to Max. Their shared history has made them a family as well as a fighting party. Max and Tanila are married, while Max's bonds with Rakonath and the demon companion allow them to share some benefits of his growth. The companions represent humans, elves, dwarves, demons, and dragons, but continue to act as one group after the climb. Those relationships now carry into a new stage in which the former climbers must create and protect peoples of their own. Their strength is collective, and the survival of each member remains bound to the choices made by the others.

The seven former climbers create a seed world under System 401, linking each founder to a people whose growth can generate divine points. Their rabbit-shaped helper explains that the group has three centuries of protection, but arena victories can transfer worlds and divine wealth. Tanila gives birth to her and Max's daughter, whose unusual connection to System magic immediately worries the family. The helper then discovers that Max's past champion kills have already ended his personal protection. He must answer an arena challenge within a week. Max grants his human bloodline to a chosen king and prepares to conceal the scale of his power. In the arena, he tests an experienced rock-bodied god before destroying him with a weapon especially effective against gods. Max refuses an offer of worlds in exchange for mercy and completes the kill, learning that Consume can take divine abilities, essence, or statistics. The decision gives him his first victory as a god but also deepens the danger surrounding Bob's power.

Max's victory brings ten worlds, millions of divine points, major betting gains, and several upgrades. He spends part of the reward on long-term improvements to soil and population growth while the founders plan how to reach the safety of higher tiers. They decide to develop their peoples through teaching, crafting, dungeons, and a future hero program. Max trains human bakers and smiths. The bound demon companion rejects his people's culture of internal violence and establishes enforceable rules for cooperation. Fowl and Batrire organize the dwarves around craft, aid, and responsible use of resources. Rakonath forms the dragons into a restrained, defensive society, and Cordelia creates Ember Grove as an open elven capital focused on knowledge and mutual protection. Max and Tanila then establish the mixed human-elven city under rules that place public welfare above divine authority. They crown the bloodline heir as its mortal king and give him a divine spark, leaving each major society with a clearer structure and common purpose.

The System helper reveals how earlier gods abused and killed him. Max and Tanila offer friendship, and he begins treating the founders as people he can trust. The group studies the costs and protections of higher divine tiers, then Max answers a request from one of his acquired worlds. In an underwater city, a neighboring aquatic goddess asks him to help defend two linked peoples from a tier-seven leviathan. She recognizes Max as a black-skill holder but accepts his claim that he does not seek indiscriminate destruction. When the invasion begins, Max uses prepared defenses and repeated lightning attacks to destroy thousands of lesser attackers. The two gods remain locked in a domain battle for eleven days. When the domain falls, Max tries to rescue the mortally wounded goddess, but the leviathan kills him during his escape. A death-prevention skill returns Max alive to Tanila and the helper, while the goddess is lost. Max survives with a sharper understanding of how completely stronger gods can overpower him.

Nearly two years into godhood, Max and Tanila's daughter is developing with unnatural speed. The founders consider another arena wager, but first Max tests demonic summoning. Instead of calling his companion, the spell carries him into the lava domain of a demon king. The summoning rules prevent the king from attacking, and his attempts leave him indebted to Max. In return for Max's restraint, the king agrees to answer a later summons and provide information. He also reveals that a higher god ordered him to protect Max's bound demon companion. Max postpones another challenge so all seven founders can grow together. Years later, he challenges a reality-altering crow god. The opponent surrenders after Max reveals that he can fly, and Max honors the surrender rather than killing for power. The resulting wealth lets the other six founders purchase bloodlines, tiers, and sparks. The group also commits to seven linked obelisks that strengthen their peoples and protect resident gods, establishing a century-long plan for shared defense and development.

The bound demon companion creates a bloodline and chooses a disciplined six-armed heir to become demon queen. Fowl and Batrire receive their own bloodlines, appoint a married dwarf healer and fighter as mortal rulers, and empower them with sparks. Cordelia grants her trauma-resistant bloodline to an elven queen who can extend protection across Ember Grove. Rakonath organizes the dragons into a guardian flight supported by the seven obelisks and considers a red wyrmling for one of its representative sparks. Years pass. Tanila strengthens the mixed kingdom through bonded mortal rulers and a network of spark-bearers, while her daughter grows into an exceptional fighter and smith despite being unable to level normally. The daughter begins hunting monsters secretly with the red wyrmling. Max observes her skill and, with Tanila, replaces prohibition with structured limits. They give her protective equipment and permission to enter low-level dungeons with trusted companions.

The founders prepare for the daughter's fortieth birthday and expected awakening. When she touches the awakening crystal, an unknown force begins crushing her life. Batrire cannot heal the damage, so Max uses demonic summoning to gain time and draws an immense entity into a sealed domain. Bob identifies it as Death, one of the Nine, and realizes the crisis is a trap. A protective mark prevents Death from seizing Max, while the summoning rules stop either side from escaping freely. Max refuses threats for nearly three months and uses the System's enforcement against Death. The entity finally agrees to return the daughter alive and awakened and to avoid acting against Max, his family, and his friends for twenty-five thousand years. Back outside, the daughter awakens with several abilities, including Blink and Ultimate Form, plus a skill that even the helper cannot read. Her survival resolves the immediate crisis, but her concealed power and the Nine's interest in black-skill holders remain unexplained.

The daughter tests Ultimate Form and joins a formal five-member champion party with the red wyrmling, a demon warrior, a dwarf healer, and an elven mage. As they begin preparing for dungeons and the Tower, Max learns that four avian gods are massacring people on one of his claimed worlds. He travels there openly and relinquishes the claim after an owl-like tier-four god halts the killing. The more aggressive falcon god then challenges him in the arena. Its speed, poison, and armor-piercing feathers force Max to reveal more abilities than planned, but he kills it and gains new divine combat upgrades through Consume. The victory leaves him questioning how broadly he can protect populations without exposing his loved ones. At home, the bound demon companion discovers that a gambling enterprise he permitted has produced debt and coercion. He closes it, compensates victims, frees three lesser offenders, and accepts their public punishment himself. Both crises push the founders toward firmer limits and more accountable rule.

The champion party defeats Max in a coordinated training exercise, then chooses to attempt two dangerous pre-Tower dungeons despite the founders' warnings. In a dragon trial, a gold dragon god offers a boon only if the group kills its red dragon member. Max's daughter refuses. An unidentified power awakens within her, lets her declare the god in breach of his own contract, and forces him to release the dragon. The two young companions accept a permanent bond that shares power and enables thought communication. The gold dragon awards the boon but says the wider game has changed. Unable to obtain answers from their helper, Max meets a trusted human god and that god's dwarven ally. Written warnings reveal that black skills are tied to a game involving the Nine and that the attention paid to Max's child is especially dangerous. The advisers urge rapid advancement. The human god also grants Max a brief, prohibited visit to his original world, where years have passed without him.

Max returns in disguise to his former faction and learns that Tom now leads it after Everett's death. Tom protects Max's secret and sends him to his family. Max finds his parents elderly, Stacy grown and raising a family, and his mother near death. Bob briefly wakes her so Max can say goodbye before the System notices and forces him to leave. Back on the founders' world, Cordelia confronts neglect and apathy in Ember Grove and accepts that generous provision without responsibility has weakened the city. Meanwhile, the champion party reaches Tower floor 55. A shadow-like boss kills the demon mage, dwarf healer, and demon warrior before the red dragon uses an escape gem to save herself and Max's daughter. Two years of grief divide the survivors until Rakonath and Max impose boundaries and make the daughter face the harm her withdrawal is causing. She reconciles with her dragon companion, selects three replacements with her, and enters the Tower again with a rebuilt party.

A world-eating void god repeats an earlier challenge against Max, apparently on another power's orders. Max refuses to surrender a world and seeks the reward owed by a world he once saved. Its elderly gnome caretaker cannot obtain a real anti-void weapon, but gives Max an imitation black-hole bomb that creates only a brief visual and gravitational effect. Max enters the arena with no reliable way to kill his opponent. He presents the imitation as genuine, then uses speed, teleportation, stored matter, and Bob's control of the arena sand to maintain the deception. The void god surrenders and admits that its father ordered both attacks, though it refuses to identify him. An arena official discovers the bluff afterward but agrees to secrecy if Max accepts the opponent's badly damaged world. The winnings let the other six founders reach tier three and Max reach tier four. Now Godbound, Max can perceive realm threads but cannot cross them without a transporter. The group delays portal construction until all seven possess tier-five domains, keeps sensitive plans private, and races toward tier six before the anticipated conflict among black-skill holders.

characters.description: A returning world champion and tower climber who leads his companions back to another world to settle an outstanding obligation. He leaves his family behind again and takes responsibility for guiding a mixed party that includes established climbers and two dragons.
characters.name: Max

characters.description: An elven climber, spellcaster, and Max's partner. She joins the expedition while carrying their child, accepting another journey away from home as part of Max's effort to settle his remaining responsibility in the other world.
characters.name: Tanila

characters.description: A dwarven climber and close companion who travels with Max as one of the expedition's frontline fighters. He is part of the established party making the waypoint journey to another world to help Max fulfill an outstanding obligation.
characters.name: Fowl

characters.description: A dwarven climber and healer who accompanies Max's party on its return to the other world. Her place in the expedition combines adventuring experience with the medical support needed by a group entering an uncertain political situation.
characters.name: Batrire

characters.description: A climber and ranged fighter who joins Max's expedition as part of his established adventuring party. She travels through the waypoint with the rest of the group as Max returns to address an obligation left in another world.
characters.name: Cordelia

characters.description: A young silver dragon bonded to Max. He travels with the expedition under the care and instruction of his red-dragon guardian. Still developing, he is absorbing an elf previously given to him and remains closely dependent on his guardian's teaching.
characters.name: Rakonath

characters.description: Rakonath's long-serving caretaker and teacher, able to take humanoid form. She agrees to leave her long-time home so she can accompany and protect the young dragon, remaining responsible for his instruction during Max's expedition.
characters.name: Red-dragon guardian

characters.description: A Golden Axe leader and ally of Max who turns day-to-day administration over to Tom so he can join the expedition. His decision places him with Max's traveling party while leaving the faction's routine operations in another trusted leader's hands.
characters.name: Everett

characters.description: A Golden Axe administrator and trainer who assumes responsibility for the faction's daily leadership while Everett is away. He stays behind rather than joining Max's expedition, providing continuity for Golden Axe during its leader's absence.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: Max's sister and the mother of Callie. An inexperienced adventurer, she fears that Max's departure may lead to another long separation. She and her daughter say farewell when Max leaves, while their parents cannot face another departure.
characters.name: Stacy

characters.description: A powerful wolfkin who seized Igarra's city and teleporter through champion challenges after killing Max's appointed champion and defeating several more challengers. His rule is firm and defiance is lethal, though local guards describe him as broadly fair.
characters.name: Igarra wolfkin champion

characters.description: A surviving local ally who serves Igarra's ruler while privately helping Max understand the champion challenge. She explains the protected preparation period, the consequence of failing to appear, and the interworld audience for the fight.
characters.name: Dark-elf administrator

characters.description: Max's bound black skill and internal adviser. Before the challenge for Igarra, he argues that greater power may be necessary for Max to protect the people he loves. His advice reaches as far as suggesting eventual godlike power, although Max rejects godhood as a goal.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: An experienced off-world dwarven crafter with thirteen crafting skills. Max secures her help making a challenge weapon, and she warns that the wolfkin ruler's metallic body may resist ordinary weapons while his axes may carry a curse.
characters.name: Dwarven weaponsmith

characters.description: A vorpal-rabbit leader allied with Max who accompanies the dark-elf administrator when Max is sent to the arena for his challenge against Igarra's ruler.
characters.name: Vorpal-rabbit leader

characters.description: Max's summoned former champion, a demon who survived defeat in a severely damaged body. Grateful that Max once spared him, he warns that every strike from the wolfkin ruler's axes adds a weakening curse.
characters.name: Bound demon ally

characters.description: A gnome power-core craft specialist who steals Rakonath's core with an unauthorized transport-and-destruction device. Her escape destroys a large part of the surrounding city, harms bystanders, and leaves the young dragon without a vital source of support.
characters.name: Gnome core thief

characters.description: A frightened member of the core thief's influential crafting family whom Max captures while searching for Rakonath's stolen core. Held alongside the thief's mother, he appears more willing to cooperate with Max than she does as the conflict widens.
characters.name: Gnome thief's stepfather

characters.description: A world-consuming challenger that claims Igarra and gives Max one day to withdraw with anyone and anything he can carry, or remain and fight. It intends to consume the world eventually, although it says the inhabitants will have years to evacuate.
characters.name: Void colossus

characters.description: Tanila's sister, identified as the zealot-linked killer behind a village massacre by the marks left on the victims. She has a power that drains victims through sustained forehead contact and is also an accomplished blade fighter. Her actions may be intended to provoke Max.
characters.name: Elven princess

characters.description: A dwarven king and former tower climber who warns that the tower's choices can permanently change people. Acting under direction from the dwarven god, he offers Max's party full-power training in a protected royal field where fatal injuries reset without lasting harm.
characters.name: Dagon

characters.description: A merfolk councilwoman who voluntarily transfers her bloodline to Max after his party wins the tournament. The transfer raises his recorded bloodline total to 60 percent, and she immediately turns to dust and dies.
characters.name: Merfolk councilwoman

characters.description: A hidden divine figure associated with Rakonath's mark who intervenes when tower watchers judge Max and Bob to be in mortal danger. He offers to pay the System's price to preserve them, warning that their deaths could endanger a prophecy and revive earlier chaos.
characters.name: Ancient god tied to Rakonath's mark

characters.description: An unnamed ruler who abducts Cordelia and threatens to kill her unless Max arrives alone within a week. The demand is intended to compel Max's surrender and creates an immediate rescue crisis.
characters.name: Elf ruler

recaps.ending: The party clears the floor-69 ocean challenge with Rakonath fighting as a tower teammate, then reaches floor 70 and defeats its cyclops boss. Rakonath is restored, stronger, and able to communicate with Max through their rank-two bond. Tanila remains pregnant and can control her royal red-skill form, though its temptation and the danger attached to their child's bloodlines remain unresolved. Fowl and Batrire remain with the core party. Everett and Tom continue supporting Golden Axe, while Stacy trains under Tom. Igarra has been surrendered to the void colossus after only willing residents were relocated. The elven princess responsible for the village massacre is still free. Bob is conscious but confined by the System after overriding Rakonath's tower eligibility, and Consume no longer works normally. Cordelia has been seized by an elf ruler after leaving with an elf ranger. The ruler demands that Max arrive alone, but Max treats the demand as a trap and prepares to take the party, Rakonath, and possibly the red-dragon guardian on a rescue. Bob still senses Max through their unbroken connection.
recaps.in_short: Max returns to Igarra, defeats the wolfkin champion who took control, and briefly resumes authority over the world. When Rakonath's core is stolen for a black-hole bomb, Max pursues the thief, dismantles the weapon, and restores the young dragon. A void colossus then claims Igarra, and Max chooses evacuation over a hopeless defense. Back home, the party crosses the tower's true threshold, learns that completion can grant godhood, and confronts the consequences of treating its inhabited worlds as disposable trials. Dagon's training strengthens the group, while Tanila gains control over her dangerous royal form. Bob forces the ineligible Rakonath into floor 69, prompting the System to imprison him and lock Consume. The party nevertheless reaches floor 70 with Rakonath as a teammate. Cordelia is then abducted by an elf ruler who demands Max come alone. Max recognizes the trap and prepares a group rescue while Bob remains imprisoned but connected to him.

recaps.text: Previously: Max became a world champion and tower climber, with Bob serving as his bound black skill and adviser. His established companions include the climbers Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia, as well as Golden Axe leaders Everett and Tom. Tanila is Max's partner and is carrying their child. Max is also bonded to Rakonath, a young silver dragon raised and taught by a protective red-dragon guardian. Max's sister Stacy and her daughter remain part of the family he is trying to protect. The companions bring different strengths to the group: Tanila is a spellcaster, Fowl fights on the front line, Batrire heals, and Cordelia attacks at range. Everett provides leadership for Golden Axe, while Tom can handle its administration and training. These relationships shape Max's continuing pursuit of strength. He remains responsible for people in more than one world and continues climbing the tower in the belief that greater power may help him keep them safe.

Max leaves Stacy and returns with his companions and both dragons to resolve his responsibility to Igarra. On arrival, he learns that a wolfkin champion has killed his appointed representative and seized the city and teleporter. The ruler is lethal toward challengers but otherwise maintains a firm order. Max hides his party and issues a challenge alone, knowing that thousands of worlds will watch. A dwarven weaponsmith helps him forge an eight-core legendary weapon capable of changing among melee forms. Max names it Sunder at the arena. The wolfkin's metal body resists most attacks, while his axes and summoned specters inflict a cumulative slowing curse. Bob eventually cleanses the curse. Max then exploits the arena's shrinking boundary, leaving the ruler trapped outside the entrance to his dimensional space. He emerges and kills the immobilized champion with Sunder, restoring his claim to Igarra. The immediate contest is settled, but the consequences of taking the world back remain unresolved.

After reclaiming Igarra, Max warns the interworld audience against future attacks. The defeated champion's body is too corrupted for Rakonath to consume safely. Max learns that his dragon bond may extend his life for centuries and that his strongest skills have advanced beyond the ranks familiar to his allies. He begins shifting Igarra toward delegated administration while exploring its trade system and local tower. Elsewhere, divine figures secretly recognize that Max controls a black skill without losing himself. The party clears the local tower rapidly, receives altered rewards because it belongs to another system, and arranges for Rakonath to remain temporarily with his guardian. Max later entrusts Rakonath's expelled core to a gnome craft specialist while supervising the work. She activates an unauthorized transport device, steals the core, and escapes in an explosion that destroys part of the city. Rakonath begins losing vital support without it. Max secures a route to the thief's world and departs alone to fulfill his promise to recover the core.

Max reaches the thief's industrial world and traces her to a powerful gnomish crafting family. He infiltrates their guarded estate, but detection ends the covert approach. After destroying mechanized defenses and taking family members captive, he clashes with a council-controlled enforcer. The thief's stepfather finally reveals that Rakonath's core is powering a weapon intended to provoke war between dwarves and goblins. Guided into a deep capital facility, Max finds the core mounted in an unfinished black-hole bomb. He defeats the augmented guards, captures the thief and her accomplices, and removes the device before local authorities arrive. The stepfather becomes a protected witness, and the council agrees to prosecute those implicated in the plot. Because no expert will risk dismantling the bomb, Max kills the thief so Consume can acquire her technical skills. He uses that knowledge to disassemble the weapon without detonating it and frees Rakonath's core. Rakonath swallows it, feels whole again, and carries Max on their first shared flight.

With Rakonath restored, the party finishes Igarra's tower alongside Max's recovering demon ally. Before Max can return home, a void colossus claims Igarra and offers him one day to evacuate or remain for an unwinnable fight. His companions persuade him to protect his family rather than die defending a world whose residents still have time to leave. Max declines the challenge and offers relocation to willing inhabitants. Eleven vorpal rabbits accompany his group home, while other allies remain behind. The red-dragon guardian then reveals the coercive threat that keeps her from their home territory and teaches Max and Rakonath that survival sometimes requires retreat. Ancient observers meanwhile identify Max as a possible disruption to a balance maintained across repeated cycles. At tower floor 60, Max's party learns that the real ascent begins there and that completion can grant godhood. Bound to secrecy, they enter a vast inhabited forest. Max negotiates with goatfolk who expect climbers to massacre them, reaches the portal without destroying their settlement, and advances peacefully to the frozen floor 61.

The party gains unusually strong rewards for completing floor 60 quickly with few deaths, then races across floor 61 and kills its ice-giant boss. Their placement reveals that other tower teams may be substantially faster. An urgent return home exposes a village massacre marked as the work of Tanila's elven-princess sister, a zealot-linked killer who may be provoking Max. Max intends to investigate without involving the wider faction. Before continuing, Dagon warns that the tower's choices can alter a climber's character and offers full-power training in a protected royal field. The dwarven king repeatedly defeats Max and reveals that royal bloodlines can grant dangerous race-specific abilities. Tanila practices a powerful gold-haired form whose intoxicating pull concerns Dagon. The full party also fails against him until it abandons direct attrition. In its final attempt, the group distracts Dagon, draws him into Max's dimensional space, and binds him where his normal advantages cannot free him. Dagon concedes, and the party returns to floor 62 determined to fight and develop together.

Floor 62 strains the party and exposes Max's tendency to protect his companions by carrying every danger himself. After an argument, Rakonath advises that overprotection can prevent growth. Max, Fowl, Cordelia, and the others reconcile and agree to face greater risks together. On the underwater floor 63, the party champions the merfolk in a three-match tournament whose losing peoples face being eaten. Fowl wins the opening contest through a carefully coordinated solo plan. Tanila uses her royal form to kill both opponents in the second match, then forfeits immediately to resist the power's seductive influence. Max wins the remaining match, ending the rival champions' rule. A merfolk councilwoman transfers her bloodline to him and dies, leaving Max with three partial bloodlines and an uncertain inheritance for his unborn child. After another boss fight, a tower evaluator reviews the lasting effects of the party's decisions across inhabited worlds. The party learns that those lives and consequences are real, and that completing the tower can create a god and found a bloodline. The evaluator also confirms that incomprehensible powers watch Max and the other black-skill holders before being forcibly silenced.

As the party approaches floor 69, Rakonath's guardian warns that his bond with Max is accelerating his growth and that separation causes him pain. Max brings Rakonath to the tower despite the dragon's lack of eligibility. Bob forces an override, allowing Rakonath inside but drawing the System's punishment. Watchers expect Bob and Max to die until an ancient god tied to Rakonath's mark pays a debt to preserve them. Bob remains confined as a lesson. Without his normal help, Max leads the party through an ocean route and a giant shark boss. Rakonath fights as a full teammate, is wounded, heals, and helps secure the victory. Consume locks, but the party reaches floor 70, and Max and Rakonath's bond advances to telepathic communication. After the next boss, Cordelia disappears with an elf ranger. An elf ruler reports that she has been abducted and orders Max to come alone or she will die. Max recognizes the demand as a trap and commits the party, Rakonath, and possibly the red-dragon guardian to a rescue. Bob remains conscious in an indestructible cell, unable to act but still linked to Max and aware of his anger.

characters.description: The returning climber who leads the effort to recover Cordelia. Max is powerful, fiercely protective of his companions, and struggling to contain his anger over the abduction and Bob's absence. He accepts Tanila's authority once the rescue party enters elven territory.
characters.name: Max

characters.description: An elven elemental spellcaster who takes charge of the rescue plan in her people's territory. Tanila is carrying Max's child and understands the dangers surrounding Cordelia's rescue. She insists that uninvolved elves must not be treated as enemies.
characters.name: Tanila

characters.description: A dwarven frontline fighter and Max's blood brother. Fowl joins the mission to recover Cordelia and urges Max to trust Tanila's judgment instead of allowing rage to dictate the party's actions. He serves as a steady restraint as well as a combat companion.
characters.name: Fowl

characters.description: A dwarven healer who travels with Max's rescue party into elven territory. Batrire is one of the five established companions at the center of the climb, providing the group with medical and magical support when its confrontations turn dangerous.
characters.name: Batrire

characters.description: Max's bonded silver dragon. Rakonath chooses to accompany the rescue even after his guardian refuses wider dragon involvement, valuing Max's willingness to let him decide freely. He provides rapid travel for the mission into elven territory.
characters.name: Rakonath

characters.description: An archer and member of Max's close-knit climbing party. At the beginning of the book, Cordelia is being held by the elves, and bringing her home is the party's immediate purpose. Her companions regard her as family and refuse to abandon her.
characters.name: Cordelia

characters.description: A red dragon who protects the surviving dragons. She refuses Max’s request for broader dragon aid because their population is small and further involvement could intensify hatred, but she leaves Rakonath free to choose his own course.
characters.name: Red-dragon guardian

characters.description: The leader of the Golden Axe and a trusted political adviser to Max. Everett sees the rescue party off and remains behind to oversee the faction and its interests, giving Max's circle an experienced administrator during a period of rising conflict.
characters.name: Everett

characters.description: A Golden Axe administrator and trainer who sees Max's party off on its rescue mission. Tom remains with the faction and Max's family while the principal climbers travel, helping maintain the home base and the practical preparations behind their expeditions.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: Tanila's father and the ruler behind the elven royal threat. He engineered a dangerous bloodline for his daughters and encouraged them to compete lethally for his approval. Tanila describes him as both an exceptional elemental fighter and a calculating strategist.
characters.name: Elven king

characters.description: Tanila's elder sister, a royal elf and formidable close-range fighter. She is the opponent Tanila intends to challenge under formal elven rules so Max can reach Cordelia. Her ability to take physical qualities from victims makes the planned duel especially dangerous.
characters.name: Tanila's older sister

characters.description: The unnamed leader of an elven faction implicated in sheltering Cordelia’s abductors. Max attacks him, prevents his escape, and takes him for questioning, but the leader’s knowledge of the abduction remains unconfirmed.
characters.name: Elven faction leader

characters.description: The two rulers of the human city. Max warns them against bloodthirsty retaliation and says Everett will replace them if they fail to govern responsibly.
characters.name: Human queens

characters.description: Max's missing adviser, held apart from him but still connected through a power-bearing bond. Bob senses the violence surrounding Max and fears that his captors are deliberately encouraging it. He cannot yet explain why he is imprisoned or why Consume remains locked.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A divine adviser who meets Max as conflict with the elves escalates. The human god warns that an elven deity may strike at Max through his allies and urges him to complete the tower quickly, while rules prevent a full explanation of Max's developing bloodline.
characters.name: Human god

characters.description: The ruler represented by a goblin image in floor 70’s flooded metal city. The city’s lifelike metal inhabitants identify him as their master and summon the party to meet him after the weather disaster.
characters.name: Goblin ruler

characters.description: A giant gnome-like construct in floor 70’s metallic upper world. It carries a staff that can alter the valley’s weather, ending a severe storm but flooding the city below.
characters.name: Giant gnome-like caretaker

characters.description: Max’s sister and Callie’s mother. Stacy is uncertain whether Callie’s father should be allowed back into their lives, and Max promises to support her decision.
characters.name: Stacy

characters.description: Stacy’s daughter. Whether Callie’s father should be allowed into her life remains Stacy’s decision, and Max promises to support whichever course she chooses.
characters.name: Callie

characters.description: A large gold dragon that attacks Rakonath’s red-dragon guardian in flight, then turns on Max when he joins the aerial battle.
characters.name: Gold dragon

characters.description: A demon bound to Max through a summoning skill. When called to inspect an anomalous coin, he recognizes its connection to a far older demonic power and safely consumes it within Max's dimensional space. Unstated protections keep a stronger rival from simply taking him.
characters.name: Bound demon

characters.description: A Golden Axe combatant whom Max carries through tower floors alongside Everett and Tom as he helps faction members advance.
characters.name: Golden warrior

characters.description: A divine relative of the fallen elven king who arrives to avenge his death. The elven goddess seizes Max and kills him while two opposing gods appear nearby. Her intervention turns the conflict from a war between peoples into a direct confrontation with divine power.
characters.name: Elven goddess

characters.description: A divine protector who joins the human god after the elven goddess attacks Max. The dwarven god helps invoke the rules that limit divine interference and recognizes the significance of Max defeating the elven king without another climber's direct aid.
characters.name: Dwarven god

characters.description: Tanila's mother and the remaining elven ruler after the king's death. With her army gone and the elven goddess excluded from the world, she is left in power for the moment because Tanila believes she may be restrained while the party returns its attention to the tower.
characters.name: Elven queen

characters.description: The mage in Stacy’s climbing party. Grella’s death leaves the group grieving and needing to regroup together.
characters.name: Grella

characters.description: A metallic System representative who appears after the party defeats the floor-79 boss. The tower host explains that the next ten floors alternate between trading opportunities and boss fights, and advises the climbers to choose their path of growth carefully.
characters.name: Tower host

characters.description: A legendary lizard craftsman whose workshop is reached when Max joins four artifact pieces. He offers to make an unusually powerful artifact in exchange for three personal prices.
characters.name: Lizard artifact crafter

characters.description: The king who rules the dwarves.
characters.name: Dagon

characters.description: Max's childhood friend and the father of Stacy's daughter. Caleb says he never received Stacy's letters and did not know she was pregnant, evidence that challenges the belief he deliberately abandoned them. Any future contact remains subject to Stacy's decision.
characters.name: Caleb

characters.description: Dagon's co-officiant in the ceremony before the party's last climb. Velda joins him in granting the five climbers a temporary divine blessing that increases their attributes for thirty days, providing practical support before they confront the final floors.
characters.name: Velda

characters.description: Max's black skill and the entity previously known as Bob. After the tower host is consumed, Consume retains a fragment of the System and Bob recovers part of his memory. The event also confirms that two other black skills are active elsewhere and farther ahead.
characters.name: Consume

recaps.ending: Max kills the tower's stronger copy of himself after the party forces it to retreat, completing the final trial. Consume takes part of the System emissary that served as the tower host, restoring some of Bob's memories and creating Max's unique Bloodline of the Consumer. Bob reports that two other black skills are farther ahead. Max, Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, Rakonath, and the bound demon enter divine adjudication. Rakonath and the demon each reject freedom and independent advancement, choosing permanent bonds with Max. The group is told it will be remade as divine champions and given worlds after a protected tutorial period. The immediate unresolved problem is numerical: eight arrivals are counted, but only seven may rule. The future of Tanila's unborn child, the other black skills, possible dragon retaliation, the elven settlement, and the friends and family left under Everett and Tom's care also remain open.
recaps.in_short: Max leads Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia from a successful rescue into war with the elven royal family and an urgent tower ascent. Tanila defeats her sister, Max kills the elven king, and divine intervention leaves the king's goddess barred from their world for a century. The party grows through dangerous tower bosses, powerful transformations, and hard choices about violence and divine patronage. All five reject offered alternative lives and enter the irreversible final floor together, aided by Rakonath and Max's bound demon. They defeat a stronger copy of Max, and Consume captures part of the System emissary, restoring Bob's partial memories and creating the Bloodline of the Consumer. At adjudication, Rakonath and the demon keep their permanent bonds to Max. The group is promised new worlds as divine champions, but eight arrivals are present when only seven may rule, while two rival black skills are already farther ahead.

recaps.text: Previously: Max is a level-one tower climber whose unusual power comes from Consume, with Bob serving as his bound adviser. His core party consists of the elemental spellcaster Tanila, the dwarven frontline fighter Fowl, the healer Batrire, and the archer Cordelia. Rakonath, a silver dragon bonded to Max, is also part of his close circle. Everett and Tom help run the Golden Axe and support the group from its home base. Max's family includes his sister Stacy. Dagon rules the dwarves. As the new volume begins, these established alliances, family ties, and tower ambitions shape the dangers ahead.

Max, Tanila, Fowl, and Batrire enter elven territory with Rakonath to recover Cordelia. Tanila takes command because the target is her elder sister's compound, and she and Fowl keep Max from treating every elf as responsible for the abduction. Tanila invokes a formal royal challenge while Max reaches Cordelia, breaks her chains, and moves her into safety. Tanila badly wounds her sister in the duel, but the defeated royal escapes to their father, the elven king. Cordelia returns home alive but traumatized and without her stolen equipment. Max gives her a powerful replacement bow and arranges support for her recovery. His anger then expands into retaliation against elven institutions. He coerces an elven faction leader into surrendering its vaults, warns the human queens against further bloodshed, and threatens wider war if attacks on his people continue. Everett reports growing fear and political pressure as the conflict moves beyond a private rescue.

Bob remains imprisoned and senses that Max's escalating violence may be serving an outside plan, while Consume stays locked. A human god warns Max that an elven deity can threaten his allies and urges him to finish the tower quickly. Max's party resumes climbing and shares new stat resources with Cordelia. On a floor divided between a flooded valley and a mechanical realm above the clouds, a goblin ruler asks them to destroy a giant caretaker. Max investigates rather than accepting either side's account. The caretaker claims that a stolen crystal sustains both its life and its duty to regulate the weather, while also accusing the ruler of using that crystal to bind the metal inhabitants. Unable to verify either story, Max enters the ruler's hidden workshop and takes the crystal and its connected pedestal for himself. An escape gem then clears the floor. The party returns home with the powerful apparatus, which Max hopes may contribute to a future dragon-tooth weapon.

Cordelia admits that captivity left her with nightmares and constant fear outside the tower. Max and Tanila make clear that she is family and give her a standing place of safety with them. Max also begins sharing the advantages of his tower access with the Golden Axe, carrying faction climbers through selected floors. Fowl's equipment and defensive abilities improve, strengthening his role as the party's tank. Max offers his sister Stacy support as she considers whether Callie's father should be found. The tower push is interrupted when Rakonath's red-dragon guardian is attacked by a larger gold dragon. Max and both allied dragons fight it in the air. Max uses his dimensional-space boundary to inflict wounds the attacker cannot heal, then kills it. Rakonath takes its heart while Max keeps its core, scales, teeth, and other materials. The victory also produces an alarming sign from Bob, who briefly reaches Max through the locked Consume connection and urgently asks for power to imprison an unidentified threat.

The party clears a huge undead boss on floor 75 by denying it loose bones, pinning it, and combining Cordelia's and Fowl's tactical support with Max's dimensional attack. The reward leaves behind a demonic coin where stored bones had vanished. Max's bound demon identifies it as a sign of an ancient and dangerous summoning power, although safeguards prevent a stronger rival from simply claiming him. The party continues through poison beetles and an ice cave, while Max helps faction teams gain levels and equipment. On floor 78, an apparently endless desert traps the party for three weeks just as an elven army advances on the human city. Everett's false rumor flushes out two likely spies. Max finally crosses the desert fast enough to locate its coastline and exit. Instead of waiting for the invading army, he decides to exploit the absence of troops from the elven capital and strike the king's seat first, with Rakonath and the red-dragon guardian supporting the operation.

The raid on the elven capital reveals that the king anticipated Max's attack. Max steals and destroys the trapped throne, then returns to defend the human city as enemy forces approach from three directions. The king's soldiers are bound into his blood magic, so every death strengthens him and pushes Max toward uncontrolled violence. Bob's active combat support returns, but Max becomes trapped inside the king's blood domain and nearly loses control of his body. He escapes the domain, defeats the king, and refuses Consume's soul-harvesting rewards. An elven goddess then arrives to avenge her relative and beheads Max. Negate Death Blow saves him. The human and dwarven gods intervene after Max survives, using System rules to force the goddess away and bar her from the world for a century. They also reveal that Tanila's unborn child is absorbing some of the parents' tower-linked power. If the party completes the climb before the birth, that inheritance could make the child unusually powerful and attract further danger.

Unknown powers discuss Max and other black-skill holders as pieces in a larger struggle. Back home, Tanila leaves her mother in charge of the elves for the present, and she and Max marry publicly. The party then returns to the tower with Bob again supporting Max. They defeat an armored beetle by attacking it from within and enter a sequence that alternates bosses with System trading floors. At a bazaar, the group acquires many objects whose uses are unclear. One of them proves essential against a teleporting stone-and-glass golem: an anchor stops its movement, allowing Fowl's defense and reflected damage to expose its core. The resulting rewards transform the party. Fowl becomes a dwarven god's Chosen, Batrire gains a much stronger body while remaining a healer, Tanila unlocks part of a bloodline, and Cordelia gains armor-like protection. Max receives the indiscriminate Wildfire spell. Everett warns that the tower's rewards are intensifying the party's desire for power, and the group recognizes the danger of continuing without restraint.

After helping Stacy face the death of a party member, Max's group reaches floor 90. The tower host explains that successful climbers can become world champions, create worlds, and establish systems, but will enter a larger conflict. All five reject an immediate alternative life under a god and choose to continue. A tailored reward gives Max the last piece of a hidden artifact. Joining its four parts takes him to a master crafter who demands three prices for an exceptional weapon: a treasured heart necklace tied to Tanila, most of Max's body, and his experience. Max pays them, though being permanently level one limits the final cost. The result is a concealed Paragon artifact forged from a dragon tooth. It can change melee forms, double Max's attributes, and harm gods with exceptional force. Max keeps its nature secret to protect the party. He then offers material help to a home for abuse survivors supported by Cordelia and gives Tanila's mother strict conditions for retaining the elven throne, including ending zealotry and rebuilding relations with other peoples.

On floor 91, Max kills a green dragon with the new artifact and Wildfire. Consume grants him wide-area illusion magic and a temporary green-dragon form, while Rakonath gains a humanoid form. Max uses the dragon's core to prepare powerful equipment for allied climbers. The party defeats an undead knight whose aura reverses healing, and Max's bound demon gains a skill through the victory. Further floors show that Max's bonds can pass unusual benefits to the demon and may also be affecting Tanila's unborn child. After floor 95, a restorative garden offers the five relief from physical and emotional scars. They reject the imposed peace and recover their full memories and feelings, passing the test. The tower host explains the endgame: floor 98 is a trade sanctuary, floor 99 offers each climber a god's alternative life, and entry to the final floor is irreversible. Even a victorious group can never return to its original world. The party reaches the floor-98 market knowing that its last decisions are approaching.

The party spends nearly three weeks trading on floor 98, gaining substantial accessories, materials, and stat increases before resisting the market's pull to remain. Fowl reaches the second stage of his progression. Back home, Bob warns that rival black-skill holders are advancing and may use Max's loved ones as leverage. Fowl defeats Dagon alone, and the dwarven king asks the group to make its last ascent from his capital. Rakonath's red-dragon guardian warns that other dragons are receiving dreams calling for retaliation over dragon deaths, but Rakonath openly chooses Max's side. Max also learns that Caleb, Stacy's former partner and Callie's father, apparently never received Stacy's letters or knew of the pregnancy. Stacy agrees only to consider a meeting. Dagon and Velda give the climbers a thirty-day divine blessing. On floor 99, Max, Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia refuse even to meet prospective patrons. They reject the offered escape route together and return home for final preparations before the irrevocable last floor.

Max crafts bonded legendary armor for Rakonath and confronts how far his pursuit of power might go. When Bob suggests killing allies or the elven queen for further gains, the party rejects sacrificing others to fear, and Max accepts their judgment. Everett and Tom take responsibility for the faction and Max's family after the group leaves. Tanila offers her mother guarded recognition while demanding that she serve the elven people better. Max, Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia enter the final floor together. The tower host becomes a copy of Max one hundred levels stronger, but the trial fails to exclude Rakonath and the bound demon. The party relies on its established roles to force the copy to retreat, and Max pursues and kills it. Consume retains part of the defeated System emissary, restoring some of Bob's memories and creating Max's Bloodline of the Consumer. At divine adjudication, Rakonath and the demon voluntarily keep permanent bonds with Max. The arrivals are promised remaking as champions and worlds of their own, but eight are present when only seven may rule. Two other black skills are also revealed to be farther ahead.

characters.description: An exceptionally powerful Level 1 tower climber who has stopped hiding behind the name Seth Pendell. Max leads Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia through floor 49 while worrying that the tower's escalating danger may outpace his ability to protect them.
characters.name: Max Hoste

characters.description: Max's sapient bound black skill and inner adviser. Bob is temporarily unavailable while undergoing an evolution, leaving Max without the guidance of the entity whose powers and appetite are closely tied to his own survival.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: Max's elven partner and a member of his tower party. She fights beside him through floor 49 and shares the risks of a climb whose difficulty is rising in response to Max's extraordinary strength.
characters.name: Tanila

characters.description: A dwarven tower climber, one of Max's closest companions, and a member of the team that clears floor 49. His place in the party is grounded in chosen family as well as their shared commitment to the climb.
characters.name: Fowl

characters.description: A dwarven healer and tower climber who clears floor 49 with Max's party. Her healing helps make the group's dangerous progress possible, though Max fears that later floors may endanger every companion who stays with him.
characters.name: Batrire

characters.description: A returning tower climber and core member of Max's five-person party. She participates in the floor-49 victory and continues with the group as it rushes through floor 50 to inspect the challenges beyond it.
characters.name: Cordelia

characters.description: One of the realm's twin queens. She acknowledges that the rulers hired a hunter to kill Max under their god's order, before they knew he carried a black skill, and is constrained from explaining protected parts of the skill system.
characters.name: Queen Molly

characters.description: One of the realm's twin queens. Alongside her sister, she confirms the divine order behind the attempt on Max's life and faces his demand for a binding promise that neither ruler will threaten his faction or friends again.
characters.name: Queen Macy

characters.description: A returning ally who led and protected Max's companions during his absence. Max considers her help a debt and promises to repay it by assisting her through the tower when the opportunity comes.
characters.name: Dexic

characters.description: The divine power associated with the human temple and the earlier order against Max. When Max activates a travel-blocking skill during prayer, the god's attempted manifestation shakes the temple and the surrounding town.
characters.name: Temple god

characters.description: Max's sister, found caring for an infant in the family's neglected home. Her circumstances show Max how sharply his family declined during his absence and intensify his resolve to watch the approaching Choosing Day.
characters.name: Stacy

characters.description: Stacy's infant daughter and Max's niece. Stacy identifies her as Caleb's child while Max offers his displaced family protection, financial support, and a safer future away from their hometown.
characters.name: Callie

characters.description: An intelligent red dragon living in a magically protected volcanic lair. Max approaches her alone because he needs a dragon capable of caring for the silver egg entrusted to him.
characters.name: Red dragon

characters.description: A newborn silver dragon who hatches under the red dragon guardian's protection. He gives Max his name, offers him a System-recognized bond, and can already communicate simple needs through their new connection.
characters.name: Rakonath

characters.description: Tanila's gold-haired sister and an apparent senior operator of the hidden facility. She arrives with armed elves, uses a coercive power against the party, and forces Max into a battle after he removes her to the desert world.
characters.name: Tanila's sister

characters.description: The captive elf whom Max fought and imprisoned. The other elves identify her as a queen when Max returns to the hidden facility.
characters.name: Elven queen

characters.description: A transformed, purple-skinned demon summoned through Max's ornate gateway during the battle with Tanila's sister. He is powerful enough that Max seeks his assistance and agrees to hear the reason for the summons.
characters.name: Sock the leg

characters.description: A temple official and former climber who once reached floor 43. Her extended life is tied to temple service, making long absences fatal, and she helps Max prepare the costly controlled summons needed to contact her god.
characters.name: Kathleen

characters.description: Fowl's unusually gifted younger brother. Tanila identifies his starting weapon-crafting talent as exceptional, raising the possibility that royal attention toward the family forge involves more than its public success.
characters.name: Grandir

characters.description: A red-haired Golden Axe leader based in Nalgren. She receives Max's party, explains the royal restrictions above tower floor 50, and offers to help them pursue lawful access while negotiating support for her faction.
characters.name: Erwinnie

characters.description: A Nalgren tower attendant who questions the party after its unusually fast low-floor clears. His interest suggests that the climbers' abilities, especially those of Fowl and Batrire, are being assessed rather than merely recorded.
characters.name: Fudamod

characters.description: The powerful dwarven king, a long-reigning monarch whose commands carry absolute authority. He receives Max's party at the castle with Fowl's parents and younger brother present, focusing the audience on Fowl and Batrire.
characters.name: Dagon

characters.description: Fowl's father, a member of the royal-forge family who is present when the king formally receives Fowl's party. The audience brings him face to face with the son who left the family and climbed beyond floor 50.
characters.name: Orstein Hammerfall

characters.description: Fowl's mother, a member of the royal-forge family attending the king's audience. Her presence makes Fowl's return to the capital both a royal matter and a confrontation with the family that rejected his path as a tower climber.
characters.name: Greta Hammerfall

characters.description: The dwarven queen, Dagon's co-ruler, and a royal host for Fowl and Batrire's wedding. She praises Fowl's rose-ore gift, recognizes Max and Fowl as blood brothers, and displays expert knowledge of dragon scales.
characters.name: Velda

characters.description: A Golden Axe leader and established ally of Max and his climbing group.
characters.name: Everett

characters.description: A Golden Axe trainer and operational leader already associated with Max's group.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: An elderly dwarven bookseller who accepts off-world books and tower records from Max. He agrees to investigate Max's unusual tower encounters in confidence.
characters.name: Sam

recaps.ending: Fowl and Batrire complete their wedding before Dagon, Velda, both families, and the assembled guests. Acting with royal authorization, Max forges Batrire a bound legendary elemental healing staff using both spouses' blood. The weapon improves her healing and has a special effect when she heals Fowl. Max is now Fowl's full blood brother, and the party remains together after clearing floor 59 and receiving several legendary advancements. Max and Tanila are engaged and expecting a child, but Tanila still fears the pressure of her newly legendary inherited skill and her dangerous royal family. Rakonath and his red dragon guardian are recovering from a rival dragon's attack, and the party plans to travel with them to another world after the wedding. The three black skills, the System's concealed history, the surviving elven harvesting network, the Watchers, and the result of completing the tower all remain unresolved. Everett's imminent work in another world is the immediate next development.
recaps.in_short: Max Hoste, formerly known publicly as Seth Pendell, learns that his black skill is one of three linked powers whose freedom threatens multiple worlds. His search for people falsely declared unskilled uncovers a hidden elven operation that has imprisoned and drained humans for centuries. Max's party destroys its System shard, captures Tanila's sister, and kills her after learning elven royalty carried the harvested elixirs. A temple god urges Max to finish the tower but warns that his loved ones may be used against him. In Nalgren, King Dagon abandons an attempt to recruit Fowl and Batrire, grants the whole party upper-floor access, and recognizes Max and Fowl as blood brothers. The party clears floor 59 and gains legendary skills, while Tanila struggles with the influence of her upgraded inherited power. Rakonath and his red dragon guardian survive a rival dragon's attack. The book ends with Fowl and Batrire married and Batrire wielding Max's legendary healing staff, while the party prepares for further tower and interworld dangers.

recaps.text: Previously: Max traveled publicly under the name Seth Pendell while becoming an exceptional Level 1 fighter and tower climber. His unusual black skill granted immense power but carried a dangerous hunger, making restraint as important as strength. Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia became his core climbing party, while Everett and Tom provided trusted Golden Axe leadership and support. Max's growing abilities drew the attention of rulers, gods, and enemies beyond his own world. He also acquired rare off-world resources and accepted responsibility for a silver dragon egg whose father had died. As the party approached the tower's fiftieth floor, Max remained committed to protecting his companions and family rather than pursuing power alone, even though the tower appeared to be shaping harder challenges around him. He had also used the celebrated identity Seth Pendell to conceal his real surname. This volume begins as he decides to live openly as Max Hoste and confront the rulers connected to an earlier attempt on his life.

Max adopts his real surname, Hoste, and leads Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia through floors 49 and 50 before pausing at floor 51. He then confronts the twin queens, who admit hiring a hunter under their god's orders and confirm that some skills can be bestowed. Their oath prevents them from explaining what happens to children declared unskilled, but they promise not to target Max or his allies again. Max repays money he gained dishonestly, arranges supplies for new adventurers, supports old friends, and asks Sam to investigate his abnormal tower encounters. The inquiry attracts a warning that someone is watching. At Windsor Wheel, Max tries to summon the human god by blocking divine travel. During the confrontation, the human god admits ordering Max's death. A stronger dwarven god intervenes, and together they reveal that Max is one of three black-skill bearers. When one grows powerful, the next is released, and all three being free could endanger many worlds. Because Max has resisted his skill's hunger, the gods suspend their effort to kill him.

Bob returns from evolution with partial memories of once being a godlike being linked to two equal siblings. He and Max acknowledge each other as friends, although Bob warns that the other black skills are growing and that powerful factions may seek control through binding agreements. Hidden conspirators also watch Max and intend for the System to kill him. Max enters his hometown in disguise before Choosing Day and discovers his sister Stacy living in hardship with an infant. Bob manipulates the local shard, and when officials falsely announce Stacy as unskilled, Max reveals himself and forces them to let her inspect her status. She actually has three strong combat skills. Max publicly confirms that he is the fighter known as Seth Pendell, reunites with his family, and exposes the lie surrounding his own Choosing Day. Questioning the responsible officials reveals that people labeled unskilled are transported to a secret site north of the capital. Max kills the senior official after extracting the lead, retains four lower-ranking prisoners, and gives his family the means to relocate safely. The town authorities agree to protect them, leaving Max ready to pursue the hidden operation.

Max repairs his family's home, then moves his parents, Stacy, Callie, and the four prisoners to the Golden Axe base. Tom begins guiding Stacy toward a defensive adventuring role while Max looks for a guardian for the silver dragon egg. In a volcanic lair, an intelligent red dragon agrees to raise the hatchling. The newborn names himself Rakonath and forms an exceptional System-recognized bond with Max before remaining with his new guardian. Back at the capital, Max gains access to rare faction materials and learns that high tower floors can connect to other worlds and even contain sapient opponents. He refuses to assume that such beings must be killed. Everett supplies a map to the politically concealed northern location. After helping Stacy train, Max's party travels toward it. A compulsion tries to turn visitors away, but most of the group resists. Beyond the affected clearing they discover a heavily defended, magically reinforced town with extensive farms and an unusually guarded central building. Max flies inside alone at night and lands unseen near the center, leaving the town's operators and purpose unknown.

Inside the hidden town, Max finds drained young human corpses and a concealed route underground. He returns with his companions, who insist on facing the danger as his family. The lower facility contains prisoners, red skill elixirs, and a shard being used to reach the System. Tanila's gold-haired sister arrives with armed elves and overwhelms most of the party. Max carries her to the desert world, where they fight beyond the facility. He summons Sock the leg, a royal-ranked demon permanently bound after three accepted summons, and eventually traps the elf in his Dimensional Space. Back at the facility, the other elves identify their leader as a queen. When the shard attacks Bob's connection, Bob evacuates the party to Rakonath's guardian. He discovers that the shard belongs to a hidden network tracking humans taken from Max's world for at least a thousand years. Bob reverses its attack and destroys it, apparently annihilating the entire hidden town. Max executes the lesser captives and questions the queen. She confirms that elven royalty transported harvested elixirs for roughly a millennium and that a tower's final floor involves a fight. A compulsion kills her before she can explain further, and Max finishes her death.

Consuming the elven queen gives Max several legendary advances and a partial royal-elven Bloodline state. Bob detects and removes a concealed cosmic tracer, showing that the queen's powers carried traps likely tied to the elven goddess. Rakonath consumes the queen's remains and equipment under his guardian's instruction. Max leaves the young dragon to continue training, while distant System overseers notice a connected threat but choose not to intervene. When the party inspects the destroyed facility, only an enormous glass-lined crater remains. Max reports the harvesting network to Everett and Tom, then seeks another controlled meeting with the temple god. Kathleen, a former tower climber whose extended life binds her to temple service, helps prepare the summons. The god accepts Max's report and says he will alert the dwarven god. He gives Max a one-use message scroll and another artifact piece, acknowledges the crisis surrounding all three black skills, and warns that other gods may use Max's loved ones to control him.
